leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight round-1 files prefer optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) as the sole prize part. All six name the same pair and describe the same core science: the magic-wavelength lattice removing the trapping-light shift, accuracy near 10^-18 reproduced across several laboratories, and uses in redshift, fundamental-constant and dark-matter tests. They differ in how they treat the open points. Several (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth) say the citation should rest on demonstrated physics and not on a redefinition of the second. Olsson and Lindroth say the priority of the magic-wavelength proposal is unchecked. Olsson also questions whether the original experiment belongs to Katori or to Ye's later, more accurate realisation. Several members say they moved to B002 after reading the openings, so this is a convergence in the files and not an independent tally. Mehlig, who lists B002 low, does not share the view.

Eriksson alone prefers topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) as a theory-plus-experiment discovery of a new state of matter, confirmed in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and 3D materials. He lists B038 and B002 as alternatives and concedes that attribution is contestable: Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang (deceased) and the 3D contributors are outside the credited trio, and the 2016 prize overlaps in subject. Mehlig lists B015 as an alternative, Danielsson questions it, and Olsson and Johansson are described as placing it seventh.

Mehlig alone prefers Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality (Kardar, Zhang, Takeuchi) as a compact, mature, conceptually central statistical-physics result with independently reproduced experimental confirmation. He lists B015 and B038 as alternatives. He states that his was the only opening ballot to place B056 and concedes that attribution is imperfect (Parisi and the exact-solution authors are outside the credited names). Kroll and Lindroth ask for evidence of reproduction beyond one liquid-crystal system and for what is independent of the 1986 theory.

areas_of_agreement: All eight files treat the Higgs experiments (B053) as a discovery of great importance. The objection to B053 is attribution (three names for ATLAS and CMS), not merit. Danielsson, who proposed it first, no longer prefers it for that reason.
Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce prefer B002 with the identical pair, and no file proposes a different pairing for B002, so the credited set is not in dispute among them.

Members who comment agree that magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B038) is real and widely replicated but not yet ripe, because the pairing mechanism is open and the first experimental author, Cao, is not among the credited names. Olsson, who opened with B038 first, accepts that her own preference has weakened.
Members who comment agree that a B002 citation should name what is new (the magic-wavelength lattice and many-atom regime) and should not rely on the pending redefinition of the second.

Several members (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Lindroth, Kroll) regard circuit QED (B017) as harder to justify so soon after the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, and as strained by the four-to-three name reduction.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus technique: Mehlig, and in part Eriksson and Pearce, ask whether lattice clocks are a discovery about nature or a precision technology. Supporters answer that the lattice regime is new and has opened redshift, constants and dark-matter tests.

Overlap with earlier prizes: Mehlig, Eriksson and Pearce in his case_against cite the 2005 (Hall, Hansch) and 2012 (Wineland, Haroche) prizes, and Ye shared 2005. Supporters distinguish the comb as a frequency ruler and ion control of single quantum systems from many-atom lattice interrogation. The members have not agreed a single sentence of difference.

Whether IceCube (B043) is sufficiently mature: Pearce and Danielsson regard the diffuse flux as secure, while Olsson and Danielsson note that source identification is thin and that only a few objects are identified.
Whether a state of matter (B015, B038) or a precision-measurement capability (B002) should be the emphasis. Eriksson raises this explicitly.

Whether the KPZ experimental confirmation (B056) is independent and broad enough: Lindroth and Kroll question reliance on mostly one liquid-crystal system, and Mehlig and Olsson say Takeuchi's status as the original experiment is unclear.
attribution_disputes: B002: no one proposes other laureates, but Lindroth, Kroll and Olsson say priority of the magic-wavelength idea (parallel proposals, for example Pottier and Lemonde) is unverified, and Olsson asks whether credit for the first demonstration belongs to Katori and for the accuracy records to Ye. Lemonde, Takamoto and the Sr and Yb community are not credited.

B053: Olsson, Mehlig, Lindroth, Kroll and Pearce question whether the three founding spokespersons or project leaders (Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee) are those who made the decisive 2012 measurement. Danielsson says they are a defensible founder trio but concedes his assessment is unverified.

B015: Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang (deceased), Fu, Moore, Hasan and Cava are outside the credited names. Eriksson says the quantum spin Hall effect can be framed around prediction and observation, while Mehlig and Danielsson say that does not dissolve the fairness issue.
B038: Cao and Dean's encapsulation work, plus earlier twistronics theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto), are outside the credited trio.
B056: Parisi and the exact-solution authors (Johansson, Spohn, Sasamoto, Amir-Corwin-Quastel) are outside the credited names.
B043: DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA pioneers are not credited with Halzen and Spiering.
B017: Blais versus Girvin for the theory slot is disputed in the four-to-three reduction, and Johansson and Kroll note they chose different names.
maturity_disputes: B002: the second has not yet been redefined and the thorium nuclear clock is still at a demonstration stage. Members say this should not delay a prize, but Johansson says he would not oppose waiting if a clearer result is imminent.
B038: Eriksson, Mehlig, Danielsson and Lindroth say the pairing mechanism is unsettled and the field is moving fast, so a prize may be early.
B043: Olsson would hold IceCube for a few years until sources are identified and credit is settled, whereas Pearce and Danielsson regard the diffuse flux as sufficiently established.
B053: all members treat the discovery as mature, and the open point is attribution, not timing.
B015: Eriksson and others describe the physics as confirmed and arguably overdue. Mehlig and Danielsson see a lineage issue with the 2016 prize.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and works in superconducting circuits, so B017 and B052 are close to his research community. He states he will recuse himself from any decision on B017 and flag B052 if it becomes decisive.

Olsson is a Fellow of the University of Tokyo (since 2025) and Katori is at the University of Tokyo, so she discloses a possible institutional connection to B002. She also notes ties to the Tohoku microscopy community (relevant to B025). She knows of no personal collaboration with Katori or Ye.

Kroll spent a year in John Hall's laboratory at JILA during his PhD and Jun Ye works in that environment. He discloses a loose scientific acquaintance and no collaboration with Katori or Ye. His Lund and WACQT affiliations are relevant to B017 and quantum-information candidates.

Lindroth discloses long-standing collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and ties to the Lund and Keller groups, none with B002 candidates. She notes AMO field loyalty relevant to B002, B052, B060 and B063.

Pearce (Chair) discloses membership of PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur, with proximity to B043 and B063, and CERN training near B053. He reports no collaboration with any named shortlisted candidate.

Mehlig notes intellectual proximity to the exact KPZ solutions through random-matrix theory, and a shared Gothenburg environment with Johansson and Olsson. Danielsson (Secretary) and Eriksson report no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: Priority check for B002: do the original papers show that Katori proposed and first demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice, and do parallel proposals (Pottier, Lemonde and others) change that, and should Lindroth and Kroll report the early-2000s chronology?

Can the committee state in one sentence what B002 recognises that the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize did not, and is that content a discovery or an enabling technique in the committee's judgement?
Should the B002 citation rest solely on demonstrated 10^-18 performance, the redshift measurement and fundamental-physics tests, without depending on a redefinition of the second?
Is B002 as a two-person prize the whole prize, or should a second distinct achievement be added, and which candidate (B015, B038, B043, B053, B033, B060, B052, B056) is the best fit and why?

For B053, can any member give a statutory argument that Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are the right three people, or is a leadership-based credit unacceptable, which would leave B053 outside the preferred configurations?
For B015 and B038, is there a defensible three-person credit given Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Cao and Dean, or does the committee regard these as not yet creditable?
For B043, is the diffuse astrophysical flux alone a sufficient discovery now, and how would the committee credit the DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA pioneers?

Johansson and Kroll disagree on the B017 theory slot (Blais versus Girvin). Given the 2025 prize and the four-to-three reduction, does any member still prefer B017 or B033, and is B060 or B033 the stronger quantum-simulation fallback?
summary.chair_observation: The files show clear convergence on B002 among six members, while Eriksson (B015) and Mehlig (B056) keep distinct preferences, each acknowledging attribution weaknesses. B002 carries the cleanest credit, and several of its supporters moved to it after the openings, so the committee should test it against its own stated caveats, namely lineage, priority and discovery versus technique, and should not read breadth of ranking as a settled result. The attribution rules for collaborations (B053) and the credit for the topological and moire topics remain open and decide which alternatives can complete a prize.
